narrative.overview: The web app is an operator's table. The phone is the notebook you carry: a white page, a few hairline-ruled cards, names set in serif, and lines you tick off. Triage is one card at a time that you clear with your thumb. Due is a page of notebook cards, one per job, with each to-do a ruled line and a checkbox. The brand comes along as one violet tint, the Band and status palettes, monospaced digits and the voice. Navigation, neutrals, SF type and appearance are left to iOS. The one loud moment is the login's brand panel, a native copy of the web front door. Inside the app there is no gradient, no glass and no shadow. Density follows Attio and Amie: tight, but not cramped. The test for every element is "does it change the decision or move a to-do?" If it doesn't, it lives in job detail.
keyCharacteristics: White systemBackground page, in light and dark alike.
Cards are a 1px separator hairline at 14pt continuous corners. Nothing is lifted.
Serif for entity names (company, today's date), SF for everything else, monospaced digits for data.
Status is a dot-label: a coloured dot on a 10% tint, with the text in .primary.
Secondary actions live in a native Menu, never in scattered inline buttons.
Snappy 0.22s motion, and nothing swaps places mid-transition.

rules.name: The One Violet Rule
rules.body: Violet means "this moves forward": Shortlist, done, ready. At most two violet moments per screen. Dismiss is slate, never red, because it's undoable and red already means a gate or Poor.

rules.name: The Dot, Not the Word Rule
rules.body: Never colour a status word. Status is a 6pt dot on a 10% tint of its hue, with the text in .primary. Orange or amber caption text fails 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Serif Is a Name Rule
rules.body: Serif is for entity names and the date masthead only. Never set a button, a label, a number or a status in serif.

rules.name: The Text Style Rule
rules.body: No hard-coded point sizes anywhere, so Dynamic Type works. The one exception is the login's decorative brand art (the role-cloud pills and the mark), which copies the web at fixed sizes.

rules.name: The Card Is the Decision Rule
rules.body: A Triage card carries exactly what one keep-or-drop call needs. Every field on it has to be able to change the decision. Description, the full breakdown, notes and contacts wait for detail.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A surface is separated from the page by a 1px separator stroke and nothing else: in light and dark, on cards, banners, chips and the round outline buttons.

dos: Do set company names and the date masthead in the system serif, and everything else in SF text styles.
Do give every card a 1px separator stroke at 14pt continuous corners on a systemBackground fill.
Do show every status as a dot-label with .primary text.
Do put secondary actions in a native Menu opened from the row or the ··· button.
Do animate toggles with .snappy(duration: 0.22), and let content fade rather than swap.
Do use .monospacedDigit() for scores, salaries, ages, counts and dates. Write dates in en-GB ("23 Oct").
Do use the CONTEXT.md words: Triage queue, Shortlist, Dismiss, Band, Gate, Chase, Task.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients, .material or .glassEffect to anything except the login panel.
Don't use grouped grey backgrounds or tonal-step cards; the page and the card are both systemBackground.
Don't colour status or Band text; Fair amber and overdue orange fail 4.5:1 at caption size.
Don't scatter "···" or text buttons across rows. One menu per row or card.
Don't hard-code point sizes outside the login's brand art.
Don't add per-Task due badges. Tasks have no dates.
Don't celebrate inbox zero: no illustration, no confetti.
